claims.claim_text: The indexed Crane Brinton is the Harvard historian who served with OSS in London and Washington.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name, NARA index entry, NARA Research and Analysis roster, and AHA memorial align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The memorial places his Harvard career before and across wartime OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Institution, profession, uncommon name, and OSS service corroborate the index identity.

claims.claim_text: Harvard University is Brinton's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation and last civilian employer.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The AHA records Harvard teaching from 1923, professorship in 1942, and wartime OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded; the source does not state a day-level leave or OSS entry date.
claims.match_notes: No intervening employer is documented; the continuing appointment is not silently ended at OSS entry.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Harold C. Deutsch is the University of Minnesota historian who led OSS research in Europe.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, index record, NARA staff roster, and Minnesota sources align.
claims.temporal_assessment: University employment began in 1929; the press biography dates OSS leadership to 1944-1945.
claims.match_notes: The institution, historical specialty, and specific OSS role provide corroboration beyond the name.

claims.claim_text: The University of Minnesota is Deutsch's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation and last civilian employer.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: University sources document faculty service from 1929 and his later OSS Research and Analysis leadership.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Harold C. Deutsch.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded; no intervening civilian employer appears in the institutional chronology.
claims.match_notes: The claim preserves the possibility of wartime leave because the sources do not specify payroll or leave dates.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Perry G.E. Miller is the Harvard historian who served as an Army major with OSS Psychological Warfare.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The full initials, rank, index record, Harvard archive biography, and NARA staff roster align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Harvard dates his resignation and Army entry to 1942.
claims.match_notes: The distinctive full name, rank, employer, and specific OSS branch identify the indexed person.

claims.claim_text: Harvard University was Miller's last civilian employer before Army and OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Harvard finding aid states that he taught there and resigned in 1942 to join the Army.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Perry G.E. Miller.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate transition from Harvard employment to Army entry.
claims.match_notes: The source explicitly distinguishes employment from the following military assignment.

claims.claim_text: Miller's immediate pre-OSS status was United States Army service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: He resigned from Harvard for the Army and was then stationed in Britain working with OSS Psychological Warfare.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Perry G.E. Miller.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence; exact assignment date is not supplied.
claims.match_notes: The Army is modeled as a military assignment, never as a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Franklin L. Ford is the historian who entered the Army and joined OSS Research and Analysis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and initial, index rank, Harvard memorial chronology, and NARA staff roster align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The memorial places a 1942 graduate semester before Army entry and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The uncommon full name and specific Army-to-OSS sequence corroborate the index record.

claims.claim_text: Ford spent one semester in graduate study at Cornell University in 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Harvard memorial places Cornell graduate study after Minnesota graduation and before Army entry.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Franklin L. Ford.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student status; the Army intervened before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Cornell is not classified as an employer.

claims.claim_text: Ford's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the United States Army.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The memorial states that he entered the Army, received a commission, and then joined OSS Research and Analysis.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Franklin L. Ford.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence; exact dates within the Army-to-OSS transition remain unknown.
claims.match_notes: Military assignment is kept separate from the unresolved last civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Gordon A. Craig is the historian whose 1941 Princeton doctorate preceded OSS work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, index entry, Stanford chronology, and NARA staff roster align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Stanford places OSS after the doctorate and Marine Corps service after OSS.
claims.match_notes: Education, profession, sequence, and exact middle initial corroborate the indexed identity.

claims.claim_text: Princeton doctoral study is Craig's probable, but not conclusively established, immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Stanford dates the doctorate to 1941 and places OSS work next in its chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Gordon A. Craig.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate; the exact OSS start and intervening months are not documented.
claims.match_notes: Princeton is represented as student status, not employment, and the chronology remains visibly qualified.

research_attempts.query_text: "Crane Brinton" OSS Harvard professor employer; NARA, professional association, university archive, scholarly, newspaper, obituary, and archival-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and unsourced derivative biographies were discovery-only; no exact leave date was inferred.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified Harvard as the best-supported immediate affiliation and last civilian employer while preserving uncertainty about leave dates.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 80 and Harvard leave records.

research_attempts.query_text: "Harold C Deutsch" OSS University of Minnesota professor employer; NARA, university records, publisher biography, newspaper, obituary, and archival-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Later faculty directories did not establish the wartime transition and were not used as sole evidence; no leave dates were inferred.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified University of Minnesota employment from 1929 and OSS leadership in 1944-1945.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 183 and University leave records.

research_attempts.query_text: "Perry G E Miller" OSS Army Harvard resigned 1942 employer; NARA, Harvard Archives, scholarly, newspaper, obituary, and archival-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Modern summary pages lacking the explicit resignation chronology were rejected as final evidence.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified Harvard as the last civilian employer and Army service as the immediate pre-OSS status.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 526 for exact Army and OSS assignment dates.

research_attempts.query_text: "Franklin L Ford" OSS Army Cornell employer 1942; NARA, Harvard memorial, university, scholarly, newspaper, obituary, and archival-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Cornell study was not converted into employment; postwar Harvard and Bennington employment was excluded from the pre-OSS field.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified a Cornell-student-to-Army-to-OSS sequence; no reliable pre-service civilian employer was identified in this stage.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 243 and pre-service records for any civilian employer.

research_attempts.query_text: "Gordon A Craig" OSS Princeton PhD 1941 employer; NARA, Stanford, Princeton, professional association, newspaper, obituary, and archival-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar Princeton and Stanford employment was excluded; the short undocumented interval after the doctorate prevents an unqualified immediate claim.
research_attempts.research_notes: Published Princeton doctoral study as a qualified probable immediate affiliation; last civilian employer remains unresolved.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 151 and Princeton records for the 1941-to-OSS interval.
